BG-1.1.translation: On the holy field of Kurukṣetra, assembled together, eager to fight...

BG-1.2.text: Marjayante mahā-bhāgā bhīṣmaṁ ca droṇam ca mādhavam
BG-1.2.translation: O Sañjaya, after my sons and the sons of Pandu assembled in the holy field of Kurukṣetra, what did they do?

BG-1.3.translation: The king's warriors and the great generals of the Pandavas were gathered.

BG-2.11.text: Aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṁ prajñā-vādāṁś ca bhāṣase
BG-2.11.translation: Your words are full of concern for bodily relatives, but those who are wise lament neither for the living nor the dead.

BG-2.20.text: Na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
BG-2.20.translation: For the soul there is neither birth nor death. All paths lead to the same truth, though they may seem different when examined.

BG-2.47.translation: Yoga is the art of right action. It is skill in all undertakings. Yoga is also defined as equanimity.

BG-2.50.translation: Give up your attachment to the results of work and surrender yourself to yoga. Steadiness is called yoga.

BG-3.19.text: Tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samācar
BG-3.19.translation: Therefore, without attachment, always perform necessary action; by doing work without attachment, one attains the Supreme.

BG-3.35.text: Śreyān svabhāvo guṇavān tat sangas tu sadoṣavat
BG-3.35.translation: It is far better to discharge one's prescribed duty, even though faultily, than another's duty perfectly.

BG-3.42.text: Indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ
BG-3.42.translation: The senses are superior to the body. The mind is superior to the senses. Above the mind is the intellect.

BG-4.7.text: Yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata
BG-4.7.translation: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice and a predominance of irreligion, at that time I descend Myself.

BG-4.13.translation: According to the three modes of material nature and the work associated with them, the four divisions of human society are created by Me.

BG-4.37.translation: Just as a blazing fire turns firewood to ashes, the fire of knowledge burns to ashes all reactions to material activities.

BG-5.10.text: Brahmany ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
BG-5.10.translation: One who performs his duty without attachment, surrendering the results unto the Supreme Lord, is unaffected by sinful action.

BG-5.24.text: Yo yaḥ sukhaḥ sarvadā sukhaḥ pare ānande gataḥ sa paramānanda
BG-5.24.translation: One who is satisfied in mind, who has conquered the senses and whose consciousness is united in the self is said to be established in yoga.

BG-6.5.translation: One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, not degrade oneself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.

BG-6.47.translation: Of all yogis, the one with great faith who always abides in Me, thinks of Me within himself, and renders transcendental loving service to Me is the most intimately united with Me.

BG-7.1.text: Mayy āsakta-manāḥ pārtha yogaṁ yuñjan mad-āśrayaḥ
BG-7.1.translation: Now hear, O son of Pṛthā, how by practicing yoga in full consciousness of Me, with all your heart, you can know Me completely.

BG-7.8.translation: I am the taste of water, the light of the sun and the moon, the syllable om in the Vedic mantras; I am the sound in ether and ability in man.

BG-9.4.text: Mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-murtinā
BG-9.4.translation: By Me, in My unmanifested form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings are in Me, but I am not in them.

BG-9.26.text: Patram puṣpam phalam toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati
BG-9.26.translation: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it.

BG-10.8.text: Aham sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate
BG-10.8.translation: I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from Me. The wise who perfectly engage in My devotional service get attached to Me.

BG-10.12.text: Tvam adi devah purushah puranah tvam asya vishnuh paramam padam tvam
BG-10.12.translation: You are the Supreme Brahman, the ultimate source of all knowledge. You are the Supreme Person, the primeval lord.

BG-11.19.text: Akhilaṁ puruṣaṁ śāśvataṁ divyaṁ adi-devam ajam vibhum
BG-11.19.translation: I see You as the eternal Supreme Personality, infinite in all directions, without beginning, middle or end.

BG-12.6.text: Ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-parāḥ
BG-12.6.translation: Those who surrender all their activities unto Me and engage in My devotional service without any mental reservation, are very dear to Me.

BG-12.13.text: Advesṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca
BG-12.13.translation: He who is not envious but is a kind friend to all living entities, who does not think himself a proprietor, who is free from false ego and equal in both happiness and distress is very dear to Me.

BG-13.2.text: Kṣetrajñaṁ cāpi māṁ viddhi sarva-kṣetreṣu bhārata
BG-13.2.translation: O son of Bharata, you should understand that I am also the knower in all bodies, and to understand this body and its knower is called knowledge.

BG-13.13.text: Jñeyaṁ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā amṛtam aśnute
BG-13.13.translation: Now I shall explain the knowable, knowing which you will taste the eternal. Brahman is beginningless and is transcendental to the material existence.

BG-14.26.translation: One who engages in full devotional service, unfailing in all circumstances, at once transcends the modes of material nature.

BG-15.1.translation: The Blessed Lord said: There is a banyan tree which has its roots upward and its branches down, and whose leaves are the Vedic hymns.

BG-15.15.text: Sarvasya cāham hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṁ ca
BG-15.15.translation: I am seated in everyone's heart, and from Me come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all the Vedas, I am to be known.

BG-16.1.translation: Fearlessness, purification of one's existence, cultivation of spiritual knowledge, charity, self-control, performance of sacrifice, study of the Vedas, austerity and simplicity are the natural qualities of work for the brahmanas.

BG-17.3.translation: O son of Bharata, according to one's existence under the various modes of nature, one evolves a particular type of faith.

BG-18.66.text: Sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekam śaraṇaṁ vraja
BG-18.66.translation: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

BG-18.73.translation: Arjuna is relieved of all his doubts and fears by the instruction of Lord Krishna on the Bhagavad-gita.

Isha-1.text: Īśāvāsyam idaṁ sarvaṁ yat kiñca jagatyāṁ jagat
Isha-1.translation: All of this is to be covered by the Lord. Whatever exists in this universe is the property of the Lord.

Isha-6.text: Yas tu sarvāṇi bhūtāny ātmany evānupaśyati
Isha-6.translation: One who sees all beings in his own self, and his own self in all beings, loses all fear.

Katha-2.1.text: Ātmānaṁ rathinaṁ viddhi śarīraṁ ratham eva ca
Katha-2.1.translation: Know the self as master of the chariot, the body as the chariot itself. The intellect is the charioteer.

Katha-2.12.text: Na jayate mriyate vā, vipariṇāmno na tasyāsti
Katha-2.12.translation: The soul is never born, and it does not die. It is unborn, eternal, permanent, and primeval.

Mundaka-1.1.text: Oṁ ity etad brahma, oṁ ity etam akṣaram brahma
Mundaka-1.1.translation: Om is Brahman. Om is all. The wise meditate upon Om continuously.

Mundaka-2.2.text: Brahmaiva satyaṁ, paraṁ brahma taj-jyotis, taj-jyotir aham asmi
Mundaka-2.2.translation: Brahman alone is the truth, the Supreme Being. I am that Brahman.

Mundaka-2.11.text: Brahmavit brahmaiva bhavati, brahmavid āpnoti param
Mundaka-2.11.translation: One who knows Brahman becomes Brahman itself. Among all the seekers of liberation, one who knows Brahman attains the highest goal.

Chandogya-3.14.text: Tat tvam asi śvetaketo, tat tvam asi
Chandogya-3.14.translation: Thou art That - the ultimate reality is the same as your innermost self.

Chandogya-6.2.text: Sad eva somya idaṁ agra āsīt, ekam evādvitīyam
Chandogya-6.2.translation: In the beginning, O dear, this world was just being, one only, without a second.

Taittiriya-2.1.translation: Brahman is Truth, Knowledge, and Infinity. Brahman is not something small, not something large.

Aiterya-1.1.text: Ātmā vā idaṁ agra āsīt, ekam eva advitīyam
Aiterya-1.1.translation: In the beginning, all that existed was the Self (Atman) alone, one without a second.

Svetasvatara-1.1.text: Athāto brahma jijñāsā, janmādy asya yataḥ
Svetasvatara-1.1.translation: Now therefore, the inquiry into Brahman: From which all beings are born.

Svetasvatara-4.6.text: Aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān, ātmā guhāyaṁ nihito yasya jānāti
Svetasvatara-4.6.translation: The Lord is smaller than the smallest and greater than the greatest. He dwells in the hearts of all beings.

Kena-1.1.text: Kenaiṣitaṁ patati preṣitaṁ manah, kena prāṇah prathamaṁ vāti
Kena-1.1.translation: By whose command does the wind blow? By whose command does the sun shine?

Mandukya-1.text: Oṁ ity etad akṣaram idaṁ sarvam, tasyopavyākhyānam
Mandukya-1.translation: Om is all this. The explanation of Om is all this world.

BS-1.1.1.translation: Now, therefore, the inquiry into Brahman (the ultimate reality).

BS-1.1.2.translation: Brahman is that from which all beings originate, by which they live, and into which they finally return.

BS-1.1.4.translation: This unity is confirmed by all the Upanishads.

BS-2.1.1.translation: The nature of Brahman cannot be anything other than what is described in the Upanishads.

BS-3.2.26.translation: According to the Upanishads, Brahman is full of bliss.

BS-4.1.1.translation: Now we proceed to explain the particular knowledge of Brahman.

RV-1.1.translation: I meditate upon Agni (the divine fire), the beloved of all, the priest of the sacrifice, the invoker, best giver of riches.

RV-10.129.text: Nāsad āsīn no sad āsīt tadānīm
RV-10.129.translation: There was neither non-existence nor existence then. There was neither the realm of space nor the sky which is beyond.

AV-10.8.translation: Salutations to Brahman, to those who know Brahman.

YV-32.1.text: Īśa vāsyam idaṁ sarvaṁ yat kiñca jagatyāṁ jagat
YV-32.1.translation: The Absolute Lord is the controller of the entire universe. Everyone is dependent on the Supreme.

SV-1.1.translation: Om is infinite bliss. Fear does not exist in the presence of knowledge of Brahman.
